q: Which cities have the worst returns and is cash on delivery the reason?
answer:
By order date: Delhi, Mumbai and Bangalore posted the largest counts of returns in September; Ahmedabad, Delhi and Noida had the highest return rates among cities with at least 10 orders.

- Largest absolute returns: Delhi — 5 returned of 57 orders (8.8% return rate; return value ₹12,283). Mumbai — 3 returned of 139 orders (2.2%; return value ₹5,252). Bangalore — 3 returned of 112 orders (2.7%; return value ₹6,235).
- Highest return rates (cities with ≥10 orders): Ahmedabad — 2 returned of 17 orders (11.8%; return value ₹3,261) — small sample; Delhi 8.8% (5/57); Noida 8.3% (1/12).
- Is COD the reason? There is a modest positive association across cities with ≥10 orders (Pearson r = 0.385) — i.e., cities with higher COD share tend to show higher return rates in this sample. Examples: Ahmedabad has COD share 47.1% and an 11.8% return rate; Delhi COD share 28.1% and 8.8% returns; Bangalore COD share 16.1% but only 2.7% returns. This means COD is likely a contributor in some cities but is not a universal explanation.
- Caveats: several high-rate cities have small order counts (sample noise); correlation ≠ causation and product mix, shipping or SKU-level issues could drive returns.

Worth checking: compare return rates by payment method (COD vs prepaid) and by top-returned SKUs in Ahmedabad and Delhi.

Period: 2026-09-01..2026-09-30 · Currency: INR · Data as of 2026-10-29
